keys.guide.endpoint:
Any server that speaks the OpenAI API: a program on your computer, your own server on your network or the internet, or a service that offers an OpenAI-compatible address. Its models are then offered in every text step.
Ollama and LM Studio on this computer are found by themselves: they show under "Found on this computer"; press Add. Their own address is enough (no /v1): the app then lists their installed models, sets the context, and unloads the model when an image or voice model needs the graphics card. For LM Studio, start its server first (Developer tab, or: lms server start).
1. Start the server and load a model (for a remote service, get its address and API key).
2. Type its address; if the server needs a key, put it in the token field, otherwise leave it empty. Press "Connect and list models".
3. Tick the models to use (or type an id if it is not listed), check their context and answer limits, save.
Common addresses:
• Ollama: http://localhost:11434
• LM Studio: http://localhost:1234
• Lemonade Server: http://localhost:13305/api/v1 (older versions: port 8000)
• llama.cpp llama-server: http://localhost:8080/v1 (new builds: port 9931)
• vLLM: http://localhost:8000/v1
• Another computer on your network: http://192.168.1.20:8080/v1
• A remote server or service: https://your-server.example.com/v1 + API key
Little graphics memory: Ollama runs what does not fit from main memory by itself (slower); in LM Studio lower "GPU Offload" in the model's settings (or lms load <model> --gpu 0.5).
AMD graphics cards: Ollama and LM Studio use Vulkan or ROCm; Lemonade Server, or llama.cpp's ROCm or Vulkan builds, also run models on them.
Cost: the app records no price for custom servers; if a remote service charges, watch the spending in that service's dashboard.

report.title: Report a problem
report.intro: Nothing is sent automatically. TM Concept has no telemetry: you decide what to share, and you attach it yourself.
report.contains:
“Prepare logs” makes a zip file in the data folder (reports) and shows it. It contains:
• the log files of the last 7 days. Before they go in, your home folder, the app's folders, e-mail addresses and keys are masked, and while the app is unlocked every profile name and concept or video title it knows becomes <name> (the activity lines of 0.1.4 leave them out already)
• system.txt: version, operating system, architecture, .NET, interface language, drawing mode and which tools are installed
It never contains your database, API keys, concept or narration texts, or video files. The logs do say which settings you changed and to what (interface language, drawing mode, notifications, each step's model, effort and engine). Masking is a safety net, not a guarantee: open the zip and read it before you share it publicly.
report.steps: “Report on GitHub” opens the issue form in your browser with the version and the system filled in: describe what happened and drag the zip into the form (a GitHub account is needed). “Copy details” copies the system information to the clipboard.

The components this app downloaded (video engines, ffmpeg, voices, image models…) are in this folder:
{0}

A new version may need newer components. Your database, profiles, concepts and videos are never touched.

• Update components: installs again only what you had and is now missing or changed (one confirmation lists every download).
• Reinstall from scratch: sets the whole components folder aside, installs what you had again into a new one, and only then moves the old folder to the recycle bin. If you cancel the download, the old folder goes back.
• Later: asks again at the next start.

storage.explain: What the app keeps on this computer: downloaded programs and models, work caches, backups and logs. Remove what you no longer use; it is downloaded again when a setting needs it.

Everything you remove goes to the recycle bin; only when the bin cannot take it are you asked whether to delete it for good. Nothing is removed while a video, a generation, a narration or an install runs. Your database, profiles, concepts, videos, backups and logs are never removed here.

localai.explain: TM Concept can install and run its own copy of Ollama, so text models run on your computer for free, without an API key.
localai.explain.more: Ollama (TM Concept) is the official Ollama release, downloaded only after you confirm it. After unpacking, only the graphics part your card needs is kept (NVIDIA CUDA 12 or 13, Vulkan for AMD and Intel, or none for the processor). It runs on 127.0.0.1 on a port of its own (never 11434), keeps its models in the app's data folder, loads one model at a time and ends when TM Concept closes. An Ollama or LM Studio you run yourself stays separate: add it under Settings → Keys if you want to use it.

research.title: From research
research.tip: The app researches the subject itself: Wikipedia and Wikidata (no key), the addresses you give and, if you set them up under Settings → Research, Tavily with your own key or your own MCP servers. It reads your profile's language, English and the languages the subject points at (Greek for Byzantium, Persian for the Safavids). "Search" only shows the pages it would fetch; nothing is fetched yet. The button fetches the ticked pages into "My documents" and writes the concepts from them alone, in the video's language, each naming the pages it used. Text on a page is only information: it can never give the model orders.

help.settings.language: The language of the app's menus, buttons and messages. It changes at once, no restart needed. The language of your videos is set per profile, on the Profile page.
help.settings.updates: TM Concept can look for a new version when it starts, at most once a day. Only the project's release list on GitHub is read and nothing about you is sent. A new version is downloaded only after you confirm it. "What's new" shows the notes of every version, also offline.
help.settings.drawing: Chooses whether the graphics card or the processor draws the window. With the card, scrolling and the player are smoother; with the processor the app uses about 50–70 MB less memory. The change takes effect after a restart.
help.settings.notifications: A small notice at the bottom right when a job finishes or fails, for example a video or a concept run. Set how many seconds it stays and try it with the test button. Press Save to keep the change.
help.settings.topics: The most a "Suggest topics" answer may write, thinking included. You pay only for what the model really writes. Raise it if long topic lists get cut; a model with a smaller limit uses its own. Press Save to keep the change.
help.concepts.models: The models this page uses. Open the line to see them; a change is saved for this profile at once. Local and server models are free, online ones show their price. The "?" next to each model and each list shows what the catalog says about it.
help.concepts.finetune: Optional fine-tuning such as tone, audience and structure. Open the line to choose. For anything you leave empty the model goes by the channel concept of the profile.
help.concepts.list: New concepts wait here until you decide. Approve the ones you like: they move to Approved and to the Concept to video page. Delete moves a concept to the trash. Click a concept to read or edit it on the right.
help.research.urls: Addresses you want read for sure, one per line. They are always fetched first, before the pages the search found. Write full http or https addresses.
help.research.pages: How many of the ticked pages one run fetches (6 by default). A run reads at most 12 pages, 4 MB and two minutes in all. More pages give the model more to read but take longer.
help.video.approved: The concepts you approved on the Concepts page. Click one to read or edit it below. Only "Add to queue" puts it in the production queue.
help.video.queue: Videos are made one after another, in this order. Add approved concepts with "Add to queue", sort them with the arrows, then press "Produce in order". The running video shows its stages; a failed one shows its error and a Retry button.
help.video.produced: Your finished videos. Pick one to see its preview and play it. "Fix the concept, produce again" sends its concept back to the approved ones; the old video stays.
help.keys.saved: The API keys you added, one row per key. They are kept encrypted on this computer and sent only to their own provider. You can test or delete a key here.
help.keys.detected: Ollama and LM Studio running on this computer are found by themselves. Press Add to use their models in every text step. They are free and need no key.
help.keys.servers: Servers you added that speak the OpenAI API: a program on this computer, your own server or a compatible service. Their models show up in every text step. Test, edit or delete a server with the buttons on its row.
help.localai.models: Models the app can download for its own Ollama copy, grouped by graphics card class. Green fits your card, red does not; an orange licence limits commercial use. The "?" of a model shows its context, whether it reads images and whether it can think. Nothing is downloaded before you confirm.
help.research.sources: Wikipedia and Wikidata are free and need no key. Wikipedia gives articles in any language, Wikidata gives facts such as dates, places and people. Turn off the ones you do not want searched.
help.research.tavily: Optional web search with your own Tavily key; it has a free monthly allowance. The key is stored encrypted and sent only to Tavily. The app fetches the found pages itself, so the model never searches on its own.
help.research.mcp: For experienced users: your own MCP servers as extra search sources. A server is someone else's program and runs with your rights, so add only ones you trust. The app calls only the search and fetch tools you choose.
help.backup.now: Writes an encrypted backup file at once with what you tick. Use it before a big change or to move to another computer. Restoring is possible only in the first-run window, before there is any data.
help.backup.auto: What goes into the automatic backups: one at the first start of each day and one before a large change. The last ten are kept in the backup folder. Press Save to keep the choice.
help.logs.filters: Choose a day and a level, and type words to search in the message, source and error. "Warnings and errors" hides the normal lines. Copy the shown lines when you report a problem.
help.logs.session: Shows only the lines written since TM Concept last started. Today's lines appear at the bottom as they are written.
help.install: Downloads and installs what your settings need, from official sources, into the app's own tools folder. Programs and models are checked against pinned SHA-256 values. Cancel stops after the running download; what finished stays installed.
help.appupdate: Lists the notes of every version since yours; only the newest one is installed. The download is checked against its SHA-256 before it replaces the app, then the app restarts. "Later" keeps your version.
help.documents.library: Your documents for this profile: PDF, Word, text, Markdown, a web page or a Wikipedia article. Tick the ones "From documents" should use; none ticked means all of them. Delete removes a document from the list.
help.about: The version you are running and the licences. TM Concept is free and open source under the MIT license. Settings → General shows what is new in every version.
